what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Every risk is already accepted: by whom, until when?
sections.para: A risk exists the moment the exposure does, so the organisation is always carrying it. There is no deny button, only three doors: accept for an interval, fund the work, or fix it, and silence escalates. Accepted differs from acceptable, every path ends at the board, and facts both establish and end each risk.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: No deny button: accept, fund or fix, with intervals
sections.para: Risks exist from the moment of exposure, unaccepted ones roll up as critical, and the interval, from four hours to six months, is the decision. Accepted is an act, acceptable a threshold the EU AI Act leaves undefined. Risks are fractal, established and ended by facts, and each material one deserves its own vault.

sections.label: A risk you are already carrying
sections.line: A risk exists from the moment of exposure
sections.para: An AI agent whose database role can write to the ledger, where some migrations cannot be rolled back, creates a risk the moment the role exists. Nobody decided to accept it. A typical register row records owner, rating and review date, but never who accepted it, until when, or what happens next.

sections.label: There is no deny button
sections.line: You cannot deny a risk, and silence escalates
sections.para: No meeting can vote a fact away, so the only choices are accept for a stated interval, fund the work, or fix it, each with a name against it. Deferral is not a fourth door. An unaccepted risk is treated as critical and rolls upward from boss to boss until somebody signs.

sections.label: The interval is the decision
sections.line: The length of an acceptance is the decision itself
sections.para: The ladder runs from one hour (get more data) and four hours (a priority-one incident) to one month (the default, fund the work) and six months (a named decision to wait). A funded acceptance lasts as long as its project. At expiry the decision returns, or the risk goes up a level.

sections.label: Accepted is not acceptable
sections.line: Accepted is an act; acceptable is a threshold
sections.para: Accepted means a named person, a date and an interval; acceptable is the point where the business stops funding remediation. Article 9(5) of the EU AI Act requires residual risk to be judged acceptable but never defines the word. Acceptance must still happen every time a risk exists.

sections.label: Every risk has a boss
sections.line: Every risk's chain of holders ends at the board
sections.para: Every holder has a boss, up to the board, and the Risk Graph Explorer vault computes what is assigned to each role and what arrives through it. Nobody may accept on someone else's behalf, and a refusal is a visible finding rather than a failure. Pushback is the point.

sections.label: From the board to the bytes
sections.line: Fractal registers link board risks down to configuration files
sections.para: A board line such as loss of customer funds opens into business, operational and technical risks, down to an agent's ledger write access. Each stakeholder accepting risk needs a register in their own words, joined by named edges. The vocabulary changes at each altitude; the grammar of holder, interval and facts does not.

sections.label: Established by facts, ended by facts
sections.line: Each risk names facts that create and end it
sections.para: In the Risk Graph Explorer, risk F-5 is established by one cited fact and ceases when F-4 or F-3 hold. The risk carries its own falsification condition, so disagreement becomes which fact is wrong. A quarterly-reviewed register row connected to nothing can be perfectly maintained and entirely wrong.

sections.label: One risk, six weeks
sections.line: One invented risk is accepted, expires, escalates and ends
sections.para: On day 1 the SRE lead accepts for two weeks; on day 15 it expires unbuilt and escalates, and the platform owner funds a month. On day 24 an irreversible migration stalls settlement, a four-hour incident. On day 42 the risk ceases on evidence, while the register row never learned any of it.

sections.label: A vault per risk
sections.line: Each material risk deserves its own evidence vault
sections.para: A vault keeps every fact, control, acceptance, escalation and incident with its history, proves it was not altered and travels as one read key. The holder writes, the chain to the board reads, and auditors or insurers get their own keys. This is a new proposal, not yet a practice.

sections.label: Twins, and where this goes
sections.line: Twins could make acceptance evidenced and risk testable
sections.para: On twins.sgit.ai every change to the risk graph, including acceptance, is made by a twin acting for a person, making acceptance the most evidenced act. Twins could also simulate risk changes. Both are designs and none is built, but they point to a register that matches reality.

sections.label: Why this is hard, and why people resist
sections.line: Executives resist the model because it disrupts their job
sections.para: RiskMandate.ai found it hard to sell: acceptance is a governance matter, not a product feature, and executives rationally resist accepting everything personally for a stated interval. Removing the deny button removes what registers are used for, and interval inflation can defeat it. It is a change programme.

sections.label: It fits alongside every GRC platform
sections.line: The model works in the gaps GRC platforms leave
sections.para: GRC platforms solve the register, workflow, frameworks and reporting, but leave gaps between rows and facts, acceptance and a clock, functions and named people. The model reads the platform's register and writes back who accepted, until when and the evidence, so vendors should sponsor and integrate it.

sections.label: What exists today, and what does not
sections.line: The model and demo vaults exist; no engine does
sections.para: The published model, RiskMandate.ai, fractal registers, the Risk Graph Explorer and the Risk Acceptance Office vault all exist. No engine yet records acceptances, runs clocks or fires at expiry, and risks.sgit.ai admits almost nothing is in code. Expiry behaviour and which ladder is canonical remain open.

sections.label: For somebody to build
sections.line: A company should run this loop; a plan exists
sections.para: The hard work is establishing risks on facts, connecting holders, running clocks, keeping evidence and guiding executives through change. The Risk Acceptance Office vault holds a business plan covering operating model, prices as hypotheses, go-to-market and first ninety days. The pitch: who accepted this, and until when?

sections.label: Sources
sections.line: Sources: the risk sites, vaults and EU AI Act
sections.para: The sources are risks.sgit.ai on the model and on accepted versus acceptable, RiskMandate.ai, graphs.sgit.ai on fractal risk registers and twins.sgit.ai. They also include the EU AI Act and its Article 9 on EUR-Lex, the Risk Graph Explorer and the Risk Acceptance Office vault.
